tb21_profile.skill: Wire several daemons into one working pipeline: sshd with password auth, a bare repo whose post-receive hook checks out two branches to two web roots, and nginx serving both over self-signed TLS
tb21_profile.domain: Linux service administration - OpenSSH, git hooks and bare repos, nginx virtual hosts and path routing, OpenSSL self-signed certificates
tb21_profile.task_form: configure-a-service end to end, graded by observed behaviour (clone, push, curl two URLs) rather than by any file's contents

verifier_notes: No grade overturned. task_003669_be3ad2e1 (TMax) is the same CD-pipeline-plus-HTTPS shape but FREE, so it is left out entirely rather than ranked. Note that this TB2.1 task's own grading is end-to-end behavioural, so `behavioral` and `strong` candidates transfer the right habit and `FREE` ones actively teach the wrong one.

tools.py search tmax '(?i)sshd|ssh server|password authentication|systemd service|reverse proxy'

Push to a local git server, validate in the hook, serve over a secure web server - the same three-stage pipeline.
Create the bare repo and a post-receive hook that builds and runs a daemon on every push; hook authorship with a strong verifier.
Git-push deployment that restarts a service automatically; the push-triggers-side-effect contract, strongly verified.
Finish a half-built staged pipeline by writing the git hook and the routing proxy - hook plus front-end routing, exactly this pairing.
Git deployment pipeline plus traffic redirection to the new version; deployment wiring with port-level plumbing.
Continuous deployment through git hooks with no root and no init system; forces the hook itself to manage the served process.
Combine git hooks, a TLS web server and a health checker; right ingredients, but graded weakly and padded with C work.
Generate a self-signed cert then stand up a gateway in front of several backend services - TLS setup plus multi-service routing.
Diagnose a 502 from nginx to its backend; the debugging loop you hit when a deployed path serves nothing.

Commit index.html and push to a bare remote; same artefacts and vocabulary, none of the service wiring.

Reproduce a staging stack: Apache with specific modules plus Varnish and Node; wiring several services into one working environment.
Build and run an sshd container with ports published; getting an SSH endpoint reachable, containerised.
Render every branch of a repository into a static HTML site - the branches-become-web-content idea, done by a tool not a hook.
Add a remote, commit index.html and push so the bare repo holds it; the client half only, strong verifier.

CLI flags and config file merge incorrectly; precedence rules between config sources, a recurring sysadmin trap.
HTTP body readers broken; protocol-level server internals rather than deployment configuration.
ssh:// remote URLs no longer resolve to a filesystem; parsing the same git@host:/path shape this task's remote uses.
Cloning over git and ssh silently does nothing; a remote operation that reports success without transferring anything.

A client uses HTTPS where the endpoint declares HTTP; scheme-versus-endpoint confusion, the same class as a wrong TLS listener.

VCS URL scheme validation for git+ssh and friends; only the URL vocabulary overlaps.

notes: Strongest corpus by far is CalibForge, which has an entire system-administration family of git-server and nginx-HTTPS-on-8443 tasks, several of them graded strong - including one (20260415_094424_002) that is essentially this task minus the second branch. TMax is a close second thanks to a large git-hook deployment-pipeline family. Terminal-Lego contributes precise single-skill pieces the others lack (nginx alias/try_files on a sub-path, self-signed cert on Apache, sshd_config override, fix ssh-to-localhost), and its verifiers here are unusually good - many strong. So yes, both new corpora beat the old ones on this task. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is usable but shallow: its Apache-with-default-ssl and push-to-a-bare-repo entries cover single ingredients, never the integration, and all are verifier-absent. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have no service-configuration tasks at all; I ranked their web-server and ssh-URL library bugs on domain, and their overall scores should be read as 'do not select these unless slots remain'. One thing the merge should know: this task grades behaviour end to end, so candidates whose own tests only check that a config file contains a string would train the wrong reflex - I preferred behaviourally or strongly verified entries at equal skill.
